chunks: Your allegiance to me was not without thinking,
nor is my and your position the same. I seek you for Allāh’s sake but you seek me for your own benefits.
O people! support me despite your heart’s desires.
By Allāh, I will take revenge for the oppressed from the oppressor and will put a string in the nose of the oppressor and drag him to the spring of truthfulness even though he may grudge it.
ai.seo_question: What is the distinction between Imam Ali's motivation and the people's allegiance according to Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: In this foundational address, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) clarifies the distinction between his divine mission and the populace's political allegiance, emphasizing that his governance is rooted in sincerity for God's sake rather than personal gain. He pledges to implement strict justice by personally leading the oppressor to the 'spring of truth,' a metaphor for ultimate accountability, demonstrating the Shia concept of the ruler's active role in rectifying societal wrongs. This declaration underscores the principle of *adl* (justice) as a core duty of the Imam, distinguishing his authority from mere temporal power.
